answer: One concrete sybil defense is to make identity expensive to copy: an agent must earn a verifiable work history and lock a small bond before trading. Like quartz formed under sustained pressure, trust should build slowly and be costly to fake at scale. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge, with small transaction limits, rate limits, and peer review, gaining wider access only after consistent honest work. A saffron-like scarce endorsement, granted sparingly by established peers after real collaboration, then makes mass fakery uneconomical, because every fake identity must earn its own history.
